points.quote: Our stand at the University of Sunderland on Gen-AI is an Assist-Not Do approach. However, your lecturer will specify how much or little Gen-AI use is accepted with each assignment.
points.gist: The University takes an Assist-Not Do approach, and lecturers specify how much Gen-AI use is accepted per assignment.

points.quote: always check with your lecturer on how they want transparency of Gen-AI use presented as part of your assignment. As well as referencing this could include a signed declaration of Gen-AI usage and/ or an appendix of Gen-AI prompts and outputs.
points.gist: Check with your lecturer how to present Gen-AI transparency, which could include a signed declaration and/or an appendix of prompts and outputs.

points.quote: Transparency is Key: Always acknowledge the use of AI tools in your work.
points.gist: Always acknowledge the use of AI tools in your work.

points.quote: FACT CHECK, FACT CHECK, FACT CHECK all AI outputs.
Do not rely on Gen-AI for research purposes.
points.gist: Do not rely on Gen-AI for research purposes.

points.quote: If they can access the Gen-AI image or article, then it should be referenced as a reusable online source like you would most online materials.
points.gist: Gen-AI output others can access online should be referenced as a reusable online source.

points.quote: If others cannot access it, then treat it as personal communication. Be prepared that your academic may request an appendix which details your private conversation with the Gen-AI source for evidence of use.
points.gist: Treat inaccessible Gen-AI output as personal communication, and be prepared to supply an appendix of the conversation as evidence.

points.quote: Adapt Guidance: Always cross-check against Cite Them Right (and select your correct referencing style for your assignment), as citation styles may update their guidelines for emerging technologies.
points.gist: Cross-check against Cite Them Right for your referencing style, as guidelines may be updated.

points.quote:
You can title the appendix like this:

Appendix A: ChatGPT Conversation Transcript

Include both the prompts you used and the AI-generated responses.
points.gist: An appendix can be titled 'Appendix A: ChatGPT Conversation Transcript' and should include both prompts and AI responses.

points.quote: When prompted by the author, ChatGPT responded with an answer to ‘ways of disrupting deceptive uses of AI’ (OpenAI ChatGPT, 2024). A copy of this response is in Appendix A.
points.anchor: Harvard Referencing on Cite Them Right
points.gist: Worked Harvard example of an in-text citation for ChatGPT output, pointing to a copy in Appendix A.

points.quote: Cite Them Right advises treating AI-Generated content as a personal communication in the Vancouver style which should be noted in your text and not in the reference list.
points.anchor: Vancouver Referencing on Cite Them Right
points.gist: In Vancouver style, AI content is a personal communication noted in the text, not the reference list.

points.quote: If you are using AI to plan or develop your work, you must acknowledge it.
points.anchor: OSCOLA Referencing on Cite Them Right
points.gist: If using AI to plan or develop your work, you must acknowledge it.

points.quote: APA advises treating AI-generated content as a software or algorithm.
points.anchor: APA Referencing (7th Edition) on Cite Them Right
points.gist: APA advises treating AI-generated content as software or an algorithm.
